key_insight: RadSight argues that reliable medical MLLM performance depends on first learning basic visual perception—like lesion location, size, and density—before higher-level diagnosis and report generation.
clinical_relevance: If validated in practice, this approach could improve the trustworthiness of AI-assisted radiology by reducing errors rooted in weak visual grounding.
method: Built Perception-Bench, a 1.13M-sample benchmark spanning 2D and 3D radiology across six tasks.
Designed RadSight with dual 2D/3D encoders to preserve native image structure.
Trained the model with a four-stage curriculum: alignment, fine-grained perception, diagnosis, and interpretation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that RadSight outperforms existing MLLMs across all six Perception-Bench dimensions and also improves on public 2D/3D medical benchmarks.
watch_item: Strong benchmark gains may not fully capture real-world clinical workflow variation, so external validation in diverse hospital settings is still needed.
paper_title: RadSight: Towards Perceptually Reliable Multimodal Radiology Image Understanding
